sections.h2: Where did Kearney, Nebraska, come from?
sections.html:
Kearney grew up beside the Platte River on the trails west, and it is the county seat of Buffalo County. In 1848 the Army built Fort Kearny a few miles southeast of today's city to protect westbound travelers. The first permanent settlement, Dobytown, stood about two miles from the present downtown, and the extra "e" in the city's name is said to have come from postal clerks who kept misspelling it.

The Union Pacific arrived in 1866, a junction with the Burlington and Missouri River Railroad was fixed in 1871, and Kearney incorporated on December 3, 1873. A year later it became the county seat. The boom that followed produced an irrigation canal, an electric street railway and a five-story opera house, and it ended with the economic crisis of the early 1890s (Wikipedia).

Buffalo County's own Register of Deeds history adds a local detail: the first courthouse stood in Gibbon in 1873, and the records were moved to Kearney at night in a wagon. The first deed recorded in the county dates to February 12, 1870.

sections.h2: How big is Kearney, and how does the highway shape it?
sections.html:
Kearney covers about 13 square miles and sits on Interstate 80, with the Great Platte River Road Archway Monument spanning the highway at mile marker 274. The Census Bureau estimates 34,782 residents as of July 1, 2025, as noted at the top of this page.

The Union Pacific main line also runs through town, and the city operates Kearney Regional Airport east of the city.

The monument's exhibits trace the Great Platte River Road from the Oregon Trail days to the present, which fits a city that began as a stop for travelers. The county reports an average commute of 16 minutes, so when you describe a house to a buyer, give the minutes to the interstate and to the university.

Health care, education, retail and manufacturing anchor the Kearney economy. Buffalo County economic development reports 34,349 employed residents, an average commute of 16 minutes, and these top employers (Grow Buffalo County):

sections.h2: How does the University of Nebraska at Kearney affect local housing?
sections.html:
UNK is a 235-acre residential campus with more than 37 buildings, and it is among the largest employers in the city. It began in 1905 as the Nebraska State Normal School at Kearney, became a teachers college in 1921, was called Kearney State College from 1963 to 1991, and joined the University of Nebraska system in 1991.

  • If you own a rental near campus, gather leases and deposit records before you talk to a buyer.
  • Central Community College also has a branch campus in Kearney.
  • Kearney Public Schools runs three preschools, ten elementary schools, two middle schools and Kearney High School, and Kearney Catholic High School is the Catholic option.

If your house is tenant-occupied, give a buyer copies of the leases and the security deposit amounts early, so there are no surprises at closing.

sections.h2: What is the weather in Kearney, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Kearney averages 25.56 inches of precipitation and 21.8 inches of snow a year, based on 1991 to 2020 NOAA normals for a station four miles northeast of town. The record high is 114 degrees and the record low is minus 30.

May is the wettest month at 4.40 inches, with June next at 3.90. Snow falls mainly from November to March, with February the snowiest at 5.6 inches. Hot summers and cold, dry winters stress roofing, siding and concrete flatwork, and a buyer's inspector will note all three.

If your house needs a roof or a furnace, get a written bid before you decide how to sell. It gives you a real number to weigh against a cash offer, rather than a guess.

sections.h2: What do Kearney's Development Services and code enforcement handle?
sections.html:
Kearney's Development Services Department combines permit services, code enforcement, inspections and planning and zoning in one place. Building Services administers the adopted zoning, building, electrical and plumbing codes, and Code Enforcement takes complaints at (308) 233-3235 or through the Access Kearney app (City of Kearney).

  • Because Building Services inspects work against the adopted building, electrical and plumbing codes, ask whether past projects on your house were permitted.
  • Residents can file a code complaint by phone or through the Access Kearney app.
  • Ask the department for open permits or violations on your address before you accept an offer.

We did not find a Kearney rule that requires an inspection or certificate when a single-family house is sold. The city code is on Municode if you want to read the chapters yourself.

sections.h2: How do Buffalo County deed recording and taxes work?
sections.html:
The Buffalo County Register of Deeds, Jen Schleusener since February 2026, records deeds in the courthouse in Kearney from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, and copies cost $0.50 a page. The office warns about a "Recorded Deed Notice" mail scam that asks for $86 and says to send no money. It also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails or texts you when a document is recorded under your name (Buffalo County Register of Deeds).

The Register of Deeds is a separate office in counties with more than 20,000 inhabitants. The same page says the state documentary stamp tax rises from $2.32 to $3.32 per $1,000 under LB1067, beginning July 18, 2026 and ending December 31, 2031. A seller pays it when the deed is recorded, so on a $250,000 house the tax is $830.

Property taxes are billed by the Buffalo County Treasurer, Brenda Rohrich, at PO Box 1270, Kearney, phone (308) 236-1250. The Treasurer's page lists tax sales among its services. Hall County's published calendar cites statute 77-204 for May 1 and September 1 delinquency in counties under 100,000 people, so ask the Treasurer to confirm the exact dates for your parcel.

sections.h2: What must a Kearney seller do about the disclosure form and its timing?
sections.html:
The disclosure statement must reach the buyer on or before the effective date of the binding contract, and the buyer must acknowledge receipt in writing. If you learn something before that date that makes the statement wrong, you must update it.

Plan for this early. Fill the form out at the start, not after you accept an offer. It covers appliances, the electrical, heating and cooling, water and sewer systems, defects that affect value, hazardous substances, title conditions and carbon monoxide alarm compliance (Nebraska Legislature).

A missed form does not void the transfer. The buyer can still sue for actual damages and attorney's fees, so complete it every time.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Kearney, Nebraska?
faqs.a: The Buffalo County Register of Deeds, located in the county courthouse in Kearney. Call (308) 236-1239 or email deeds@buffalocounty.ne.gov.

faqs.q: What is the Nebraska documentary stamp tax rate for a Kearney sale?
faqs.a: It is $3.32 per $1,000 of value from July 18, 2026. The Buffalo County notice says the increase runs through December 31, 2031.

faqs.q: What is the Recorded Deed Notice scam in Buffalo County?
faqs.a: It is a mailer that asks for about $86 for a copy of a recorded deed. The Register of Deeds says copies cost $0.50 a page at the courthouse and that people should not send money.

faqs.q: Does Kearney require a point-of-sale inspection for a house?
faqs.a: We did not find one for single-family homes in the city pages we reviewed. Call Kearney Development Services at the number on the city's code enforcement page to confirm.

faqs.q: Which school district covers most of Kearney?
faqs.a: Kearney Public Schools, which operates preschools, ten elementary schools, two middle schools and Kearney High School.
